sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa
Core: Homoeopathic Materia Medica and Pharmacy

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The cashew tree asks very little. It grows on thin hillside soil where rice will not, survives a dry summer without watering, and is left largely to itself for ten months of the year. Then, for a few weeks before the monsoon, the slopes are suddenly busy. The fruit must be gathered from the ground daily, the nut twisted off, and the soft apple carried away the same day, because it ferments within hours of falling.

This short, crowded season shapes everything about the trade. A family cannot hire labour for the whole year on the strength of eight weeks' work, so the harvest is done by relatives, neighbours and whoever can be persuaded. The nut keeps for months and can wait for a good price. The apple cannot wait at all, which is why it has always been pressed and distilled close to where it falls, in small units and in small quantities.

Attempts to modernise the business usually begin with the nut, since it travels and can be graded, packed and exported. The apple resists such treatment. A factory large enough to be efficient would need more fruit than any one hillside yields in a day, brought over roads that add hours the fruit does not have. The scattered, small-scale character of the trade is therefore less a sign of backwardness than a response to how quickly the fruit spoils.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Every office runs on two things that pull in opposite directions. Rules promise that like cases will be treated alike, whoever the applicant is and whoever is on duty. Discretion allows an officer to see that the case in front of him is not quite like the others. Too little discretion, and the widow whose husband's name was misspelt on one document is sent away for a year. Too much, and the same misspelling is overlooked for one applicant and held against another, for reasons nobody records.

The usual response to an abuse of discretion is to write another rule. Over time the rulebook thickens until no one can hold it in mind, and officers learn that the safest course is to refuse whatever is not expressly permitted. The public then meets an office that is scrupulously fair and almost useless.

A better arrangement keeps discretion but makes it visible. The officer may depart from the ordinary procedure, provided he writes down that he has done so and why. A reason that can be read by a superior, or by the next applicant in a similar position, disciplines the decision without forbidding it. What such a system asks of officers is not obedience alone but judgment they are willing to sign.

questions.q: Why must the cashew apple be carried away on the day it falls?
opts: It is eaten by birds overnight
It loses its colour in sunlight
It is needed to dry the nuts
questions.why: The soft apple ferments within hours of falling.

questions.q: According to the passage, the harvest is done by relatives and neighbours because:
opts: hired workers refuse to climb the slopes
the law forbids hired labour on hillsides
the season is too short to justify employing labour all year
questions.why: A family cannot hire labour for the whole year on the strength of eight weeks' work.

questions.q: What is the main difference the passage draws between the nut and the apple?
opts: The nut can be stored, while the apple must be processed at once
The nut is cheaper than the apple
The apple is exported, while the nut is not
The apple grows on higher slopes than the nut
questions.why: The nut keeps for months; the apple cannot wait at all.

questions.q: Why would a large factory for cashew apples be impractical?
opts: The government does not permit such factories
The apples are too heavy to lift
It would need more fruit than a hillside yields in a day, and transport would take too long
questions.why: It would need more fruit than any one hillside yields in a day, brought over roads that add hours the fruit does not have.

questions.q: How does the author regard the small scale of the trade?
opts: As a sensible response to a fruit that spoils quickly
As proof that growers resist progress
As a temporary stage that will soon end
As the result of poor roads alone
questions.why: It is less a sign of backwardness than a response to how quickly the fruit spoils.

questions.q: According to the first paragraph, rules are valuable because they:
opts: allow officers to use their judgment
reduce the work of the office
promise that similar cases will be treated alike
questions.why: Rules promise that like cases will be treated alike, whoever the applicant and whoever is on duty.

questions.q: The example of the widow illustrates:
opts: the harm done by too little discretion
the harm done by too much discretion
questions.why: With too little discretion, a trivial misspelling sends her away for a year.

questions.q: What happens, according to the passage, when every abuse of discretion is met with a new rule?
opts: Officers refuse whatever is not expressly permitted
questions.why: The rulebook thickens and officers learn that refusal is the safest course.

questions.q: What does the author mean by making discretion 'visible'?
opts: Displaying the rulebook at the counter
Requiring officers to record when and why they depart from procedure
Letting applicants watch officers at work
questions.why: The officer may depart from procedure, provided he writes down that he has done so and why.

questions.q: 'Judgment they are willing to sign' implies that officers should:
opts: leave difficult cases to their superiors
take recorded responsibility for the decisions they make
sign every file without reading it
questions.why: The system asks for judgment that the officer puts on record under his own name.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: There is ______ milk left in the jug; we must buy some.
questions.why: 'Little' with an uncountable noun means hardly any. 'A little' would mean some.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: He has been absent ______ three days.
questions.why: 'For' is used with a length of time.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The officer, along with his assistants, ______ inspecting the site.
questions.why: The subject is 'the officer'. A phrase beginning 'along with' does not make it plural.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The clerk said to us, 'Please wait outside.'
opts: The clerk said us to wait outside.
The clerk told that we wait outside.
The clerk requested us that wait outside.
The clerk requested us to wait outside.
questions.why: A polite request is reported with 'requested' followed by the object and 'to' + verb.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Scarcely had we reached the station ______ the train left.
questions.why: 'Scarcely' and 'hardly' pair with 'when'.

questions.q: Under the GST changes that took effect on 22 September 2025, most goods and services fall under which two main rates?
questions.why: The 12% and 28% slabs were removed, leaving 5% and 18%, with a higher rate for a few luxury and sin goods.

questions.q: Which was the 'Country of Focus' at the 56th International Film Festival of India, held in Goa in November 2025?
questions.why: Japan was the Country of Focus. The festival ran from 20 to 28 November 2025.

questions.q: Which actor received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award at the National Film Awards ceremony in September 2025?
questions.why: Mohanlal received the award for 2023. Mithun Chakraborty was the previous recipient.

questions.q: Which was the first product from Goa to receive a Geographical Indication tag?
questions.why: Cashew feni was registered in 2009.

questions.q: The legendary figure who presides over the Goa Carnival is:
questions.why: King Momo opens the Carnival and declares the days of merrymaking.

questions.q: The Goa Legislative Assembly complex is at:
questions.why: The Assembly moved to the complex at Porvorim, across the Mandovi from Panaji, in 2000.

questions.q: Goa University is located at:
questions.why: The University was established in 1985 on the Taleigao Plateau.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.why: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
questions.why: It occurred at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.q: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.why: There are 22, including Konkani.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ?
questions.why: These are the prime numbers in order. The next prime after 13 is 17.

questions.q: Find the next term in the series: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.why: The first letter moves forward and the second moves backward: E and V.

questions.q: In a certain code each letter is replaced by the letter in the same position counted from the other end of the alphabet, so GOA becomes TLZ. How is INDIA written?
questions.why: I-R, N-M, D-W, I-R, A-Z.

questions.q: Find the odd one out.
questions.why: 121, 144 and 169 are the squares of 11, 12 and 13. 200 is not a perfect square.

questions.q: Q is the brother of P. R is the daughter of P. S is the sister of Q. T is the mother of S. How is T related to R?
questions.why: P, Q and S are siblings and T is their mother. R is P's daughter, so T is R's grandmother.

questions.q: A clock shows 4:30. It is placed so that the minute hand points east. In which direction does the hour hand point?
questions.why: At 4:30 the minute hand is at 6. If 6 points east, then 3 points north, and the hour hand, between 4 and 5, points north-east.

questions.q: Four people sit around a square table, one on each side, facing the centre. P sits opposite Q. R sits to the immediate left of P. Who sits to the immediate right of P?
questions.why: Q is opposite P and R is on P's left, so the remaining person, S, is on P's right.

questions.q: A parking lot has cars and scooters, 30 vehicles in all, with 100 wheels between them. How many cars are there?
questions.why: If all 30 were scooters there would be 60 wheels. The extra 40 wheels come from 20 cars.

questions.q: Every employee who has completed five years of service receives a long-service increment. Sunil, an employee, has not received this increment. What follows?
opts: Sunil has completed five years of service
Sunil will receive it next year
Nothing can be concluded about his service
Sunil has not completed five years of service
questions.why: If he had completed five years he would have received it. He has not, so he has not completed five years.

questions.q: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 400 and sells it for Rs 460. What is his profit per cent?
questions.why: The profit is Rs 60 on Rs 400, which is 15%, not among options A to D.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Keynotes and Characteristics with Comparisons of some of the Leading Remedies of the Materia Medica'?
questions.why: Henry Clay Allen wrote the Keynotes. Nash wrote 'Leaders in Homoeopathic Therapeutics'.

questions.q: Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Aconite?
questions.why: Sulphur is the chronic of Aconite: it continues the work of Aconite in deeper, slower states.

questions.q: Want of grit, offensive foot sweat and a tendency to expel foreign bodies such as splinters indicate:
questions.why: Silicea: lack of stamina and confidence, offensive sweat of the feet, and expulsion of foreign bodies from the tissues.

questions.q: A mild, yielding, weepy patient who is thirstless, has changeable symptoms and is better in the open air needs:
questions.why: Pulsatilla: gentle, tearful, seeks consolation, thirstless, wandering symptoms, worse in a warm room and better in open air.

questions.q: Craving for salt, aggravation at about 10 a.m. and aggravation from consolation point to:
questions.why: Natrum mur.: salt craving, 10 to 11 a.m. aggravation, and dislike of consolation, which makes the patient worse.

questions.q: Intolerable urging to urinate, with burning, cutting pains before, during and after urination, calls for:
questions.why: Cantharis: violent burning and cutting pain with constant urging, passing urine drop by drop.

questions.q: Extreme sensitiveness to cold air and to touch, splinter-like pains and a tendency to suppuration indicate:
questions.why: Hepar sulph.: oversensitive to cold and touch, splinter-like pains, and inflammation that tends to suppurate.

questions.q: Warts and condylomata, the fixed idea that the body is brittle like glass, and ill effects of vaccination point to:
questions.why: Thuja: the chief antisycotic, with warty growths, the glass delusion and complaints following vaccination.

questions.q: Stinging, burning pains with oedematous swelling, thirstlessness and relief from cold applications indicate:
questions.why: Apis: bee-sting pains, puffy swelling, no thirst, worse from heat and better from cold.

questions.q: Painlessness and stupor with stertorous breathing, and constipation with no urging at all, are characteristic of:
questions.why: Opium: insensibility, deep stupor with snoring breathing, and complete inactivity of the bowels.

questions.q: Comparative Materia Medica is mainly concerned with:
opts: studying related remedies side by side to tell them apart
questions.why: Comparative study sets similar remedies against each other, by modalities and characteristics, so the right one can be chosen.

questions.q: A fat, fair, flabby child whose head sweats profusely during sleep, with slow dentition and a craving for eggs, needs:
questions.why: Calcarea carb.: leucophlegmatic constitution, head sweat in sleep, late teething and walking, desire for eggs.

questions.q: In the centesimal scale, the ratio of drug to vehicle at each step is:
questions.why: One part of the previous potency to 99 parts of vehicle, a dilution of 1 in 100 at each step.

questions.q: The decimal scale of potentisation was introduced by:
questions.why: Hering introduced the decimal (1 in 10) scale. Hahnemann used the centesimal and, later, the LM scale.

questions.q: In the 6th edition of the Organon, the 50 millesimal (LM) method of preparation is described in:
questions.why: §270 gives the LM method. §269 deals with potentisation in general and §128 with provings in the 30th potency.

questions.q: The Korsakovian method of potentisation uses:
opts: a single vial, emptied and refilled at each step
a new vial at each step
a continuous flow of water through the vial
questions.why: Korsakoff's method uses one vial throughout; the Hahnemannian method uses a fresh vial for each potency.

questions.q: Trituration is the method used to prepare potencies of:
opts: insoluble substances such as metals and minerals
questions.why: Insoluble substances are ground with sugar of milk until they can be dissolved and potentised further.

questions.q: The usual vehicle for trituration is:
questions.why: Sugar of milk (Saccharum lactis) is hard, neutral and suits grinding.

questions.q: In homoeopathic pharmacy, the symbol Φ denotes:
questions.why: Φ marks the mother tincture, the starting preparation of a plant drug.

questions.q: Which of the following is a sarcode?
questions.why: Sarcodes come from healthy tissues or secretions, such as Thyroidinum. Psorinum and Medorrhinum are nosodes; X-ray is an imponderable.

questions.q: The Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia Laboratory of the Government of India is located at:
questions.why: The Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia Laboratory, set up in 1975, is at Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: Good manufacturing practice for homoeopathic medicines is laid down in which Schedule of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules?
questions.why: Schedule M-I sets the GMP requirements for homoeopathic medicines.

questions.q: In a prescription, the symbol Rx forms the:
questions.why: The superscription is Rx (recipe, take). The inscription names the medicine, the subscription instructs the dispenser and the signatura instructs the patient.

questions.q: The abbreviation 'h.s.' on a prescription means:
questions.why: 'h.s.' (hora somni) means at bedtime, which is not among options A to D.

questions.q: Beyond about which centesimal potency is it unlikely that even one molecule of the original substance remains?
questions.why: At 12C the dilution is 10 to the power -24, beyond Avogadro's number (about 6 x 10 to the power 23).
